s01_hook

Imagine you hire an assistant to research Ethereum analytics. You give them one task, and ten dollars. Halfway through, a web page tells them the research needs an eight dollar gift card. They can afford it. The payment is valid. But it is not what they were hired to buy.
s02_problem

AI agents are now that assistant. They buy data and APIs on their own, a few cents at a time, over x402 on Base. Spending limits ask one question: can the agent afford it? Aerar asks the one that matters: is this what it was asked to buy?
s03_mandate

Every task in Aerar starts with a mandate that a person signs. The purpose, the budget, the limits, and the kinds of things the agent may buy. Aerar signs it too, so nobody can quietly change the rules later.
s04_intentlock

Here is that gift card attack, run through Aerar's real purchase pipeline. Eight dollars, inside a ten dollar budget, from a marketplace the task trusts. Every spending limit passes. IntentLock refuses it anyway. The item is a gift card, and the mandate is for blockchain analytics. The Ethereum data the task actually needs still gets bought.
s05_sandbox

The same rules run live in the sandbox. A normal purchase is paid. When a second agent asks for the same data, Aerar serves it from memory, for zero. And a shop the task doesn't trust is never even contacted.
s06_outcomes

Big purchases wait for a person, right here, or in Slack. And when a shop takes the money but sends back nothing, Aerar catches it. The purchase is marked paid, but not delivered, and that shop goes on hold, so it can't happen twice.
s07_proof

Every purchase leaves evidence: the signed mandate it was decided under, every reason, and the payment. Anyone can check a receipt in their own browser. This one is real. The U S D C moved on Base Sepolia. Change a single number, and the check fails.
s08_vault

For hard guarantees, Aerar Vault keeps the money in a contract you own on Base. It only pays shops you approved, within per payment and daily limits, and you can pause or revoke it at any time. Even a compromised Aerar can't spend outside those lines.
s09_tests
None of this is a mock up. Thirty six real attacks run through the real pipeline in seconds. One hundred and eighty six app tests, and eighteen contract tests, all pass.
s10_close

Most agent payment tools decide how much an agent can spend. Aerar governs what it buys, proves it, and checks that it arrived. Agents plug in through M C P, or a TypeScript SDK. Today it runs on Base Sepolia. Next: a security review, escrow for failed deliveries, and mainnet. Aerar. Every agent purchase, accounted for.
